topics.topic: Deterministic aggregation, multiplicity, ordering, and attribution of same-stage refusal failures
questions: When several checks in one stage fail, is the refusal's kinds list ordered, are repeated occurrences of one kind preserved, and how is each failure associated with the input that caused it?
When several failures in one stage have the same kind, does the refusal list that kind once or once per failure, and in what order are multiple kinds returned?
What exact, deterministic failure list is returned when several checks in the same stage fail, including multiple fields failing with the same kind?
When the import is closed and another stage-(6) condition also fails, does the answer contain every stage-(6) failure or only `import_closed`?

quotes:
An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
of that stage (A04 rule 6).
Stage (1) comes first — the session, the CSRF value and the confirmation value, used up when it was carried (A13 rule 6) — and this refusal comes before every other of the import's own checks.
judgement.why: The State 5 convention requires all failures in the first failing stage, while the reviewed import flow gives import closure priority over every other import check.

bases.passage:
An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
of that stage (A04 rule 6).
bases.rests_on: When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them.

bases.passage: Stage (1) comes first — the session, the CSRF value and the confirmation value, used up when it was carried (A13 rule 6) — and this refusal comes before every other of the import's own checks.

unsupported_sides: Stage (1) comes first — the session, the CSRF value and the confirmation value, used up when it was carried (A13 rule 6) — and this refusal comes before every other of the import's own checks.

witness.initial: Owner sessions A and B each hold an uploaded file, and B holds a valid confirmation for its file.
events: Session A confirms an import successfully.
The accepted import records the closure and drops every owner session's uploaded file.
Session B submits its still-valid confirmation.
outcomes: The first passage returns stage (6) kinds `import_closed` and `file_not_kept` together.
The second passage returns only `import_closed`, because that refusal precedes the other import checks.
witness.observer: The owner in session B and the owner-interface caller see different refusal data.
basis: An accepted import drops the uploaded file of every owner session (M11); a confirmation shown in another session is refused because the import is closed (rule 8).
While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused (R0-79).

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie browser persistence and lifetime attributes
questions: What persistence attribute is set when the cookie is first issued: is it a browser-session cookie, a persistent cookie, or a cookie with no Registry-defined lifetime beyond browser policy?
Must the sign-in response create a browser-session cookie with no Expires/Max-Age attribute, or a persistent cookie, and if persistent what lifetime represents “never expires”?
Must the owner-session cookie survive closing and reopening the browser while its server-side owner session remains valid?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the owner-session cookie's browser persistence and lifetime attributes.

precedent.topic: Owner session cookie persistence and lifetime
quotes:
Registry never expires or deletes the cookie: an ended session's
cookie is refused at the session check and replaced by the next sign-in, so
no answer, however late it arrives, can remove a newer session's cookie.
precedent.why: Whether the HTTP cookie carries Expires or Max-Age is a public contract and wire-format detail owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Facts included for rooms and artifact pointers in import mapping output
questions: Which facts of each room and artifact pointer are included in the mapping output?
Which facts of every imported room and pointer must `read_import_mapping` return?

quotes:
At `mapping`, the mapping: the picked projects by `project_id`, each one's rooms and
pointers in their lists' orders, the name and alias each arrives under, the
Customers it will make by their v1 value with the projects each links, every
malformed record of the picks, every id of a record the picks bring in that
production already holds — no other production id — and every missing
value; and whether the mapping is clean — no malformed record, no conflict,
no missing value and at least one pick — which alone lets the confirmation
step be shown.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns only room and pointer identity/status information, while another returns the complete room and artifact-history projections including references, digest, owner service and instants; the owner reviewing the import mapping notices the difference.
judgement.why: The operation fixes the collections and their order but not the facts each room or pointer entry contains.

witness.initial: An accepted upload contains picked project P, room R, and a published estimate pointer E with a URI, digest, owner service, version and source instants.
events: The owner requests the mapping for P.
outcomes: The mapping shows R and E only by identifiers and basic status or version.
The mapping shows every fact exposed by `projects.list_rooms` and `artifact_pointers.list_pointers`, including E's reference, digest, owner service and instants.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing what the import will bring in.
basis:

for `mapping`, the picks — possibly none — each with the display name and
alias it arrives under, and for each Customer the import will make its
name, its kind and whether the v1 value is its tax id.

topics.topic: Conflict handling when duplicate project picks specify different values
questions: If one project is supplied more than once with different display names, aliases, or associated Customer values, which values does the single resulting pick use, or is the request refused?

quotes:
The read transaction; the mode, `upload` or `mapping`; the file's bytes;
for `mapping`, the picks — possibly none — each with the display name and
alias it arrives under, and for each Customer the import will make its
name, its kind and whether the v1 value is its tax id.
judgement.divergence: One implementation keeps the first values supplied for the duplicated project, while another keeps the last values or refuses the conflict; the owner sees a different mapping and may confirm a different imported project.
judgement.why: Treating picks as a set does not determine how conflicting values attached to duplicate occurrences are resolved.

topics.topic: Owner-interface route and method mapping and rejection behavior
questions: Which owner-interface routes and methods exist, which page or action does each invoke, and how are an unknown route and a disallowed method answered?

judgement.why: Concrete HTTP routes, methods, route-to-action encoding and transport responses for unknown routes or methods are wire-contract and format details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Whether sign_out_owner admits an untrusted session identity or receives an admitted session
questions: Does sign_out_owner receive only an already-admitted session, making no_owner_session impossible for this operation, or does it receive and validate an untrusted session identity itself?

quotes:
The admitted session: the step of a sign-out request, which
`admit_owner_request` runs holding the import lock and the session's lock.
`unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`) when no valid session is named.
judgement.why: The input contract permits only an already-admitted session, while the error contract requires `sign_out_owner` itself to encounter an invalid or absent session.

bases.passage:
The admitted session: the step of a sign-out request, which
`admit_owner_request` runs holding the import lock and the session's lock.
bases.rests_on:
Validity is
checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).

bases.passage: `unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`) when no valid session is named.

unsupported_sides: `unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`) when no valid session is named.

witness.initial: The browser carries a cookie for an owner session that has already ended.
events: The browser submits a sign-out request.
outcomes: `sign_out_owner` receives the invalid session identity and returns its declared `no_owner_session` error.
